classification.tone: Grounded, cerebral, emotionally raw, and increasingly uncanny

evaluation.positioning_hook: A high-achieving college sophomore with a dead mother and a loaded mind starts time-traveling through trauma to uncover the truth behind her family.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has a clean emotional engine — a brilliant young woman, a dead mother, a campus mystery, and a time-bending investigation — that can be pitched quickly and emotionally. The college setting, romantic tension, and supernatural mystery broaden the lane beyond pure genre.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early: Jessica sees a black void on campus, gets pulled into a mystery around Henry Maddox, and discovers she can move through time via emotional states and writing. The script keeps the rules elastic, but the central engine is easy to track.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Jessica is a strong lead because she’s both hyper-competent and emotionally brittle, which gives an actor range and the story real friction. Kerri, Maddox, Henry, and Susan each bring a distinct pressure point around her, creating a durable character web.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script takes a bold swing by turning trauma processing into a literal narrative technology, with creative writing as the mechanism of control. The voice is confident, literate, and willing to be funny, horny, academic, and frightening in the same breath.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The story keeps escalating through campus discoveries, temporal slips, and emotional confrontations, with each episode ending on a strong turn. The momentum is strongest when Jessica is actively investigating; the more theoretical passages slow the engine a bit.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The idea of a perfectionist student using story, theory, and emotional dysregulation to access time travel feels fresh and immediately legible. The script’s best invention is that the supernatural and the psychological are never separate systems.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Morgan College feels specific, social, and alive: elite liberal arts culture, dorm gossip, Discord mythology, steam tunnels, old yearbooks, frat-house history, and faculty power dynamics all feed the story. The campus is not just a backdrop; it’s the machine that generates the mystery.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is unusually specific: intellectual, profane, emotionally exposed, and lightly satirical, with sudden horror imagery and campus-comedy rhythms. The script can pivot from a joke about grade inflation to a black void monster without losing its voice.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Beneath the time-travel premise is a layered story about grief, identity, authorship, sexual power, and the stories families tell to survive. The pilot and follow-on episodes suggest a much larger emotional and thematic architecture than the surface mystery alone.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: Jessica/Kerri is a strong friendship engine, Jessica/Maddox is loaded with manipulation and need, and Jessica/Henry carries attraction, danger, and metaphysical intrigue. Even secondary figures like Donovan and Susan create meaningful pressure on the central triangle.

casting_characteristics: Lead requires a female actor in her late teens/early 20s playing a high-achieving college student
Supporting roles include a Korean-American student, an African-American imagined figure, and a young mother in her early 20s
One child role for Jessica at around age 10 and one little girl role in the time-slip sequence

notable_requirements: College campus with dorms, library, lecture hall, quad, dining hall, and administrative office spaces
1999 period dressing, props, and vehicles for time-travel sequences

technical.vfx_details: Temporal shifts, overlapping realities, disappearing characters, black void monster, and reality-warping transitions require compositing and enhancement.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical blood effects, monster attack beats, environmental transformation cues, and possible makeup/prosthetic work for injury moments.

rights_flags.detail: Krzysztof Penderecki’s 'Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima' is specifically named and used as a story/scene cue.
Twilight, Prius, iPhone, Discord, Reddit, Doctor Strange, and Matrix are referenced by name.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming feature or premium-cable/limited theatrical genre-drama lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model with strong festival-to-platform potential; the story is serialized in feel but the submitted material reads as a feature-length narrative.

cost.note: The footprint is campus-contained and mostly interiors, but the period work, VFX reality shifts, and monster imagery push it above microbudget.

cast.note: The project depends on a strong young lead and a compelling professor role, with additional identity-specific supporting parts and child casting in key flashback material.

location.note: A college campus, steam tunnels, frat house, hospital, apartment building, and 1999 period inserts create variety without becoming globe-trotting.

content.note: Sexual coercion implications, suicide imagery, profanity, and mental-health material narrow the lane to mature audiences.

rights.note: The script uses a handful of named songs, brands, and pop-culture references that will need standard clearance review.

strengths.what_it_means: The role gives an actor intelligence, vanity, vulnerability, comic timing, and emotional collapse in one package. She’s the kind of protagonist who can carry a prestige genre feature because the audience wants to watch her think, break, recover, and keep going.
strengths.evidence: Jessica’s drunken Martin Eden recitation, her campus panic, her confrontations with Maddox, and her final emotional plea to the hedge-monster.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The campus is a story engine.
strengths.what_it_means: Morgan College is rendered as a social ecosystem with class markers, gossip channels, faculty power, dorm mythology, and institutional memory. That gives the script a vivid, producible world that feels specific enough to market and rich enough to sustain a feature.
strengths.evidence: The Discord chatter, yearbook vandalism, steam tunnels, frat-house lore, and Maddox’s role on the admissions board.

strengths.what_it_means: The script turns emotional dysregulation into a literal mechanism for time travel and reality slippage, which makes the concept feel both inventive and thematically unified. That’s the kind of high-concept logic buyers can grasp fast and actors can play truthfully.
strengths.evidence: Jessica’s Penderecki-fueled self-induction, the black monster, and the overlapping realities in the dorm and campus spaces.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The professor role has dangerous charisma.
strengths.what_it_means: Maddox is not just an exposition machine; he’s seductive, manipulative, grieving, and intellectually dominant. That’s a premium supporting role for a name actor who wants to play authority with menace and grief underneath.
strengths.evidence: His private office sessions, the journal, the “feel it” doctrine, and the final wrist-grab confession that his son is dead.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The friendship dynamic is commercially warm.
strengths.what_it_means: Kerri gives the script a grounded, funny, emotionally legible counterweight to the metaphysics. She’s the friend who can call Jessica out, protect her, and keep the movie human between the bigger swings.
strengths.evidence: Their drunken banter, Kerri’s skepticism, the absinthe party, and the repeated “I need you” / “I’m here” exchanges.

strengths.dimension_or_area: It blends prestige and genre cleanly.
strengths.what_it_means: This can play to audiences who want a smart, emotionally literate drama and to viewers who want a mystery with supernatural propulsion. That hybrid lane is attractive because it widens the buyer conversation without flattening the material.
strengths.evidence: Freud, Lacan, and Joan Didion sit in the same script as a black void monster and a time-slip frat house.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The mother story gives it real ache.
strengths.what_it_means: The emotional core is not just “solve the mystery” but “understand the mother who left.” That gives the feature a universal hook beneath the genre mechanics and makes the ending feel earned rather than merely clever.
strengths.evidence: Jessica’s flashbacks, the phone call with her father, the bird-sanctuary vision, and the final plea to the hedge as “Mom.”

strengths.dimension_or_area: The writing has a confident, literate voice.
strengths.what_it_means: The dialogue is sharp, self-aware, and rhythmically alive, with a voice that can move from campus comedy to psychological horror without sounding generic. That voice is a calling card for a writer and a reason to pay attention.
strengths.evidence: The Martin Eden bit, the “plot vs character” exchanges, and the recurring jokes about theory, therapy, and academic performance.

whats_special.headline: This is a smart, emotionally charged genre feature with a real lead role at its center and a campus world that feels alive enough to franchise. The script’s best move is making trauma, authorship, and time travel part of the same engine — which gives producers a marketable hook and actors something substantial to sink into.

lead_characters.name: Jessica Wolfe
lead_characters.hook: Jessica is a hyper-competent overachiever with a cracked emotional center: brilliant, funny, self-mythologizing, and secretly terrified that her mind is betraying her. She’s the kind of young woman who can quote literature while drunk, weaponize intellect in a fight, and still collapse into childlike need when the truth gets too close. The role lives in contradiction — control versus chaos, ambition versus grief, skepticism versus belief — and that contradiction is the engine.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a showcase part for an actor who wants range, specificity, and a real emotional arc. It offers the kind of material that can pivot from sharp comic campus energy to raw breakdown and back again, with the same appeal as the lead performances in 'Eighth Grade' and 'The Worst Person in the World' in terms of interiority and volatility.

lead_characters.name: William Maddox
lead_characters.hook: Maddox is a brilliant, handsome, deeply unsettling professor who speaks in therapeutic riddles and treats emotional pain like a discipline. He’s paternal, predatory, wounded, and persuasive all at once — a man who can make manipulation sound like wisdom and grief sound like pedagogy. He’s the story’s dark intellectual center, and every scene with him carries charge.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a prestige supporting/lead-adjacent role with authority, mystery, and menace. It gives an actor the kind of layered, scene-stealing material that lives in the same dramatic space as Paul Dano in 'There Will Be Blood' or Michael Stuhlbarg in 'Call Me by Your Name' — intelligent, emotionally loaded, and quietly dangerous.

lead_characters.name: Kerri
lead_characters.hook: Kerri is Jessica’s best friend and reality anchor: blunt, funny, socially fluent, and emotionally loyal without being sentimental. She’s the person who can puncture Jessica’s self-seriousness, protect her in public, and still make the friendship feel lived-in and affectionate. She brings the movie its oxygen.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a juicy best-friend role with real comic timing and emotional function. It gives an actor the chance to be the audience surrogate, the skeptic, and the loyalist all at once — the kind of part that can pop the way Beanie Feldstein does in ensemble friendship material.

lead_characters.name: Henry Maddox
lead_characters.hook: Henry is boyish, needy, intelligent, and unstable in a way that feels both seductive and tragic. He’s the kind of young man who can flirt, deflect, and self-destruct in the same breath, and he carries the story’s romantic and metaphysical charge. He’s not just a love interest; he’s a living clue.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a strong young-actor role because it asks for charm, fragility, and volatility. It has the emotional and tonal complexity that can launch a performance in the same lane as Timothée Chalamet in 'Beautiful Boy' or Lucas Hedges in 'Manchester by the Sea' — sensitive, damaged, and magnetic.

lead_characters.name: Susan
lead_characters.hook: Susan is Jessica’s mother before the myth hardened: impulsive, charming, messy, and emotionally opaque. She reads as a real young woman with a life outside motherhood, which makes her both more human and more haunting when Jessica encounters her across time. The role carries the ache of seeing a parent before the wound.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a compact but memorable role with emotional resonance and a strong reveal. It gives an actor the chance to play warmth, ambiguity, and a touch of danger, in the spirit of the younger-parent material in 'Aftersun' or 'Lady Bird' flashback dynamics.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make a smart, emotionally intimate genre film with real visual invention.
director_appeal.detail: The material rewards a filmmaker who can balance psychological realism with uncanny imagery and keep the emotional point of view locked to Jessica. It offers room for elegant campus atmosphere, subjective reality shifts, and a final act that can feel both mind-bending and deeply personal.

buyer_appeal.lane: Prestige genre / elevated sci-fi drama / campus mystery
buyer_appeal.detail: This fits a lane that likes smart, actor-forward genre with a contained footprint and a distinctive voice. It’s producible without globe-trotting scale, but it still has enough concept, mood, and emotional stakes to justify a theatrical or premium streaming push.

considerations.area: The script’s strongest lane is elevated genre, not broad commercial horror.
considerations.detail: The material is most persuasive when positioned as a prestige psychological mystery with supernatural elements and a strong female lead. That framing protects the emotional intelligence of the piece and helps buyers understand the audience.

considerations.area: The campus world could support a very clean production footprint.
considerations.detail: A focused location plan around dorms, offices, tunnels, and a handful of period inserts would keep the movie efficient while preserving the specificity that makes it feel expensive on the page.

considerations.area: The time-travel rules stay deliberately fluid.
considerations.detail: A future pass could sharpen the audience’s sense of what Jessica can do, when she can do it, and what triggers the shifts, while keeping the emotional mystery intact. The current version already has the right feeling; a little more rule clarity would make the engine even more propulsive.

considerations.area: Maddox’s authority is the story’s most volatile pressure point.
considerations.detail: The dynamic is compelling because he can be mentor, manipulator, and grief-stricken father in the same scene. One direction would be to keep foregrounding the emotional cost of his guidance so the audience always feels why Jessica keeps returning.

considerations.area: Kerri is the audience’s grounding wire.
considerations.detail: Her skepticism and loyalty are doing important work, and the friendship already plays well. Expanding a few more beats of their private shorthand would deepen the emotional contrast when Jessica drifts into the uncanny.

considerations.area: The 1999 material gives the feature its most cinematic lift.
considerations.detail: The period details, analog tech, and pre-digital social texture create a strong visual and emotional contrast with the present. Leaning into that contrast will make the time-slip sequences feel more tactile and memorable.

considerations.area: The ending lands on a strong emotional door-open.
considerations.detail: Jessica choosing to step back into Maddox’s office after everything she’s seen gives the feature a clean, unsettling final turn. That’s a strong place to end because it promises both danger and deeper revelation.
